title: Claude runtime-started turns: host ownership, result attribution, detected/unmediated record and continuity drift
outcome: A turn Claude Code starts by itself is owned, attributed and recorded truthfully by the host, and its result can never finish, checkpoint or credit another turn
acceptance: A Claude turn that the runtime starts by itself is identified from the stream by the probed contract — on a runtime that advertises msg_lifecycle_v1, turn output that no command_lifecycle `started` and no result identity ties to an outstanding host prompt, normally after a task_notification; on a runtime without it, init, then turn output with no exact echo of an outstanding host prompt before it — adopted under its own host owner and generation shared by the prompt writer and the stdout reader, shown Active while it runs, and host prompts sent meanwhile queue behind it; a test replays the probed frame sequences through the production frame router.

A result finishes only the turn it is correlated to — on a lifecycle runtime, the one host prompt its user_message_uuid(s) name; on a runtime without lifecycles, the turn whose init and echo opened it: a runtime-started turn's result never finishes, checkpoints, retries, or clears the replay prompt of a host-dispatched turn, including when a host prompt is written while the runtime-started turn runs; an uncorrelated or unresolved result never finalizes any grant, an error result with no correlated owner never puts an Idle session into Error, and a subagent's frames never reset or finalize the root turn; tests cover these schedules through the production frame router.

A runtime-started turn is recorded as detected and unmediated: the transcript shows an immediate mediation-gap notice when it is adopted, and its commands, tests and source changes are never attributed to another turn's grant or credited; a test shows it.

Continuity drift is tracked apart from a turn's own measured begin: when a workspace's actual begin basis differs from the previous checkpoint's end basis for the same workspace and run/root binding, the host records the drift with both revisions and the previous checkpoint reference and surfaces it as a host diagnostic, while the turn's own begin basis stays the measured one; a test shows drift with a no-edit next turn and no drift when unchanged.
The full gate passes on the landed input.
The /review-changes pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium or higher finding on the reviewed input.

A result finishes only its correlated turn. Such a turn is recorded as detected and unmediated, with an immediate mediation-gap notice, and nothing of it is attributed or credited to another grant. Continuity drift is tracked apart from a turn's measured begin. Retained Claude work reaches checks and carried gates through one interference rule (src/engram_claude_interference.rs): registration against each check's evidence interval, a carried run fenced outright up to its first terminal read and judged per settlement candidate by its own closure after that, and reconciliation at the publication cut.
